title: The youth department's reports against the City's payment table
question: How much of what the City paid out through the youth department do the year-end reports account for?
finding: The reports account for $104.7 million spent in 2024-25 and $104.1 million in 2025-26. The City's payment table shows the department (code CHF) paying $138.1 million and $139.8 million under those year labels ($135.1 million and $139.8 million by the year of the voucher number), so the reports cover about 76% and 74% of it. Payments by the department peaked at $179.0 million in fiscal 2023 (by voucher year) and were $110.7 million in fiscal 2019.
how: Report spending is the sum of every strategy table in the 2024-25 and 2025-26 year-end reports. City payments are every voucher line with department code CHF (the Department of Children, Youth and Their Families), summed by the year on the line and, separately, by the year its voucher number belongs to (scripts/lib/vouchers.py).
limits: The department may pay for work outside these service-area reports, and the reports do not say what share of its payments they cover; a grantee's reporting year and the City's fiscal year may not line up. The gap is a question about what the remaining payments bought, not a finding that money is missing. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days.
